correctness.rationale: All definitions are exactly those of Jiang Sections 2.1 and 10. There are 24 states and six cyclic classes. The q=0 chain has fast, strictly aperiodic intra-class rotation dynamics. Each one-break configuration is enumerated, proving exit coefficients 9/16, 7/12, 7/4; label equivariance and the impossibility of reversing a cyclic orientation in a one-break move imply identical rates to four adjacent classes. Standard finite-dimensional singular perturbation gives generator a(A_oct-4I) at times floor(t/q), t>0. Its 0,-4a,-6a eigenspaces give the displayed exact two-exponential total variation profile and the mixing-time limit. The attached exact-rational checker executed 7,471 assertions and 18 finite-q consistency tests; finite tests are supplementary, not the limit proof. Boundary t=0 and epsilon>=5/6 explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The primary source gives theta(1/q) mixing-time divergence and finite adhesion tables, but not exact first-order generators, the six-class octahedral quotient, sharp three-implementation constants, or total-variation limiting profile. Older clumpy shuffled-label chains and nonsticky GSR families differ in transition laws. Searched published indexed mathematical records on four-card adhesive mixing and neighboring models; no matching or stronger implication was identified, subject to nonexhaustive historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial four-card cyclic-orientation quotient provides a natural six-state state space; exact high-adhesion mixing constants for three widely compared implementations go beyond known order bounds and the source finite table. The two-exponential TV profile captures two distinct macroscopic relaxation modes and determines every fixed tolerance below the fast-layer level. The exact rate ratios distinguish physically different release conventions and are not a textbook substitution, arbitrary numerical slice, or already tabulated statistic.
